title: Impact of Vietnam Service on Long-Term Earnings

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Instrumental Variables (2SLS), using the Vietnam draft lottery number (z) as an instrument for actual Vietnam service (x).
- Why: Draft eligibility was as-if randomly assigned by lottery and strongly influenced service, while not directly affecting long-run earnings except through service.
- Estimand: LATE of Vietnam service on log earnings for compliers (those whose service status responds to draft assignment).
- Key assumptions:
  1) Relevance: z shifts the probability/intensity of service (Cov(z, x) ≠ 0).
  2) Independence: z is as-if random and independent of potential outcomes and unobservables affecting earnings.
  3) Exclusion: z affects long-run earnings only via x (no other channel).
  4) Monotonicity: No defiers (nobody serves less because they are assigned to be drafted).
  5) SUTVA: No interference and a well-defined treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Required packages
need <- c("AER","sandwich","lmtest")
have <- rownames(installed.packages())
for(p in setdiff(need, have)) install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
library(AER)
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s69_data.csv")
# Ensure proper types
df$z <- as.numeric(df$z)
# Rename control to avoid backtick quoting in formulas
df$controls_var <- df$controls

# Quick sanity checks on instrument balance and relevance
cat("Sample size:", nrow(df), "\n")
cat("Mean x by z (first-stage check):\n")
print(tapply(df$x, df$z, mean))
cat("Mean y by z (reduced-form check):\n")
print(tapply(df$y, df$z, mean))

# 2) Naive OLS (ignoring endogeneity)
ols <- lm(y ~ x + controls_var, data = df)
ols_vcov <- vcovHC(ols, type = "HC1")
ols_ct <- coeftest(ols, vcov = ols_vcov)
ols_b <- coef(ols)["x"]
ols_se <- sqrt(diag(ols_vcov))["x"]
ols_p <- ols_ct["x","Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("\nNaive OLS (y ~ x + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_OLS = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            ols_b, ols_se, ols_b - 1.96*ols_se, ols_b + 1.96*ols_se, ols_p))

# 3) First stage: x on z + controls; report coefficient and partial F for z
fs0 <- lm(x ~ controls_var, data = df)
fs1 <- lm(x ~ z + controls_var, data = df)
fs1_vcov <- vcovHC(fs1, type = "HC1")
fs1_ct <- coeftest(fs1, vcov = fs1_vcov)
fs_bz <- coef(fs1)["z"]
fs_sez <- sqrt(diag(fs1_vcov))["z"]
fs_pz <- fs1_ct["z","Pr(>|t|)"]

# Partial F-stat for excluded instrument z
anova_fs <- anova(fs0, fs1)
# Extract F-stat and p-value for adding z
fs_F <- anova_fs$`F`[2]
fs_Fp <- anova_fs$`Pr(>F)`[2]
cat("\nFirst stage (x ~ z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on z = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4f\n", fs_bz, fs_sez, fs_pz))
cat(sprintf("  Partial F for z = %.2f (p = %.4f)\n", fs_F, fs_Fp))

# 4) Reduced form: y on z + controls
rf <- lm(y ~ z + controls_var, data = df)
rf_vcov <- vcovHC(rf, type = "HC1")
rf_ct <- coeftest(rf, vcov = rf_vcov)
rf_bz <- coef(rf)["z"]
rf_sez <- sqrt(diag(rf_vcov))["z"]
rf_pz <- rf_ct["z","Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("\nReduced form (y ~ z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  Coef on z = %.4f, SE = %.4f, p = %.4f\n", rf_bz, rf_sez, rf_pz))

# 5) 2SLS main: y ~ x (endog) + controls | z + controls
iv_main <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls_var | z + controls_var, data = df)
iv_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_main, type = "HC1")
iv_ct <- coeftest(iv_main, vcov = iv_vcov)
iv_b <- coef(iv_main)["x"]
iv_se <- sqrt(diag(iv_vcov))["x"]
iv_p <- iv_ct["x","Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("\n2SLS (main) (y ~ x + controls | z + controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            iv_b, iv_se, iv_b - 1.96*iv_se, iv_b + 1.96*iv_se, iv_p))

# 6) Robustness A: No controls
iv_noc <- ivreg(y ~ x | z, data = df)
iv_noc_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_noc, type = "HC1")
iv_noc_ct <- coeftest(iv_noc, vcov = iv_noc_vcov)
iv_noc_b <- coef(iv_noc)["x"]
iv_noc_se <- sqrt(diag(iv_noc_vcov))["x"]
iv_noc_p <- iv_noc_ct["x","Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("\n2SLS (robustness A: no controls):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            iv_noc_b, iv_noc_se, iv_noc_b - 1.96*iv_noc_se, iv_noc_b + 1.96*iv_noc_se, iv_noc_p))

# 7) Robustness B: Quadratic in control
df$controls_var2 <- df$controls_var^2
iv_quad <- ivreg(y ~ x + controls_var + controls_var2 | z + controls_var + controls_var2, data = df)
iv_quad_vcov <- vcovHC(iv_quad, type = "HC1")
iv_quad_ct <- coeftest(iv_quad, vcov = iv_quad_vcov)
iv_quad_b <- coef(iv_quad)["x"]
iv_quad_se <- sqrt(diag(iv_quad_vcov))["x"]
iv_quad_p <- iv_quad_ct["x","Pr(>|t|)"]
cat("\n2SLS (robustness B: quadratic in control):\n")
cat(sprintf("  beta_IV = %.4f, SE = %.4f, 95%% CI = [%.4f, %.4f], p = %.4f\n",
            iv_quad_b, iv_quad_se, iv_quad_b - 1.96*iv_quad_se, iv_quad_b + 1.96*iv_quad_se, iv_quad_p))

# 8) Wald ratio check (without controls): RF/FS
# For comparability with no-controls 2SLS, compute RF and FS without controls
rf_nc <- lm(y ~ z, data = df)
fs_nc <- lm(x ~ z, data = df)
wald_beta <- coef(rf_nc)["z"] / coef(fs_nc)["z"]
cat("\nWald ratio (no controls): RF(z->y)/FS(z->x) = ", sprintf("%.4f", wald_beta), "\n", sep = "")

# Final clear numerical result print (main 2SLS estimate)
cat("\n==== Main Causal Estimate (2SLS with controls) ====\n")
cat(sprintf("LATE of Vietnam service on log earnings: %.4f (SE = %.4f)\n",
            iv_b, iv_se))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Negative. Veterans drafted and serving in Vietnam are expected to have lower long-run earnings due to foregone civilian experience, disrupted education, and potential health impacts.
- Magnitude: For log earnings, an IV estimate around -0.10 to -0.20 is plausible (i.e., 10–20% lower earnings for compliers), typically larger in magnitude than naive OLS which is biased toward zero due to positive selection into service avoidance and negative selection on unobservables. Robustness checks should preserve sign and be of similar magnitude, with a meaningful first-stage F-stat (>10).

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Use draft lottery number as an instrument for Vietnam service.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Military service during the Vietnam War positively affects long-term earnings.
